# Thinking it through

I've been working this 7.7 mu for 40 years now. My body isn't what it used to be — my back aches in the morning and I can't carry fertilizer bags like I did at 40. But I know this land better than most men know their wives. I know the northwest corner dries out first, the strip along the ditch holds water three days longer, and the middle block is where the wheat always looks best at jointing.

My household has five — me and my wife, my son and his wife when they're not away working, and my grandson who's in middle school. That's enough hands for most things, but for cotton picking in September-October I still have to hire some help from the next village.

I keep 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's our grain, that's food security, and after 40 years it's what I know best. The other 2.7 mu I put to cotton. I've thought about dropping the cotton because the price isn't what it was fifteen years ago and picking is hard on my back, but the cash matters and that piece of land has been cotton for many years; the soil suits it.

## Wheat (5 mu, planted last October, harvesting June)

Target yield about 450 kg/mu — that's realistic for my ground. I went in last October with 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15 compound as base, which gave me 6 kg N/mu plus my P and K. These fields have been farmed continuously for decades so the P and K are built up; I don't need to overdo it. Now in spring at jointing I'll topdress 22 kg/mu of urea — another 10 kg N — for a total around 16 kg N/mu. That matches what my fields actually need.

Irrigation: I already did the pre-winter watering in late November. I'll irrigate at jointing (now, basically), then at heading, then probably at grain filling if May is dry. Three to four times total. Each one costs me about 40 yuan/mu in electricity and pump time. It's a lot, but without water on this plain the yield collapses by half — no choice.

I'll spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading. Harvest by combine, hired — 60 yuan/mu, worth every fen because I can't swing a sickle anymore.

## Maize (5 mu, planting mid-June right after wheat, harvesting late September)

The turnaround from wheat harvest to maize planting is maybe 5 days — tight. I hire the no-till seed-drill operator; he comes through the village with his tractor. 30 yuan/mu and it saves me a week of tillage. Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the agro-shop has in stock — around 50 yuan/mu. Plant density about 4000 per mu.

Base fertilizer 30 kg/mu compound at planting, then topdress 15 kg urea at big trumpet stage. About 14 kg N/mu total. Target 500 kg/mu.

Irrigation: maize usually gets summer rain, so often I only need one irrigation around tasseling if July is dry. Sometimes two. I'll spray once for borers if I see egg masses.

## Cotton (2.7 mu, planting late April, picking September-October)

This one takes the most work and the most pesticide. I buy Bt seed — about 50 yuan/mu — which cut my insecticide spraying way down compared to twenty years ago, but I still spray 4-5 times for mirid bugs and aphids, probably 150 yuan/mu across the season.

Fertilizer I split three ways: base at planting with compound fertilizer (20 kg/mu), at squaring with urea (12 kg/mu), and at flowering with another 10 kg urea/mu. About 12-13 kg N/mu total. Cotton doesn't need as much N as maize — too much N and it grows leaves instead of bolls.

Irrigate twice usually — once after squaring starts if May-June is dry, once at peak flowering. Pruning and topping through the season to keep the plant architecture right.

Picking is the hard part. My wife and I start the first pick ourselves in early September, then I hire 3-4 people from the village for the main flush — maybe 8-10 hired-days total across 2.7 mu.

## What I'm not doing

I'm not chasing maximum yield. Every extra bag of fertilizer is money I might need for my blood pressure medicine or if the pump motor burns out. I'd rather hit a steady 450 kg wheat and 500 kg maize every year than gamble on 550 and risk losing it. At 70, stability matters more than squeezing the last few kg.
